protocol: 3 rounds x 3 proposals; one positive scoring winner at most per round

descriptor_candidates.name: confine_ratio_L
descriptor_candidates.hypothesis: Entropy loss scales with confinement tightness: adsorbate entropy loss is governed by the ratio of pore-limiting diameter to molecular diameter, modulated by the pore volume-to-surface-area ratio; a descriptor combining log(lsd_p/lsd_f) with Vol/LabuteASA lowers MAE of s_ads/s_gas residuals versus the 14-input baseline network.
descriptor_candidates.rationale: Inference (not source evidence): tighter confinement (small lsd_p relative to lsd_f) restricts translational and rotational degrees of freedom, so entropy loss should grow with the confinement ratio; Vol/ASA acts as an effective pore channel diameter controlling how much of the adsorbate motion is suppressed.
descriptor_candidates.falsification_criteria: If adding this descriptor to the 14-input network does not reduce held-out MAE of entropy loss/R by a statistically significant margin (e.g., >5% improvement with overlapping error bars on resampling), or if residuals anti-correlate with the descriptor, the confinement-ratio mechanism is falsified for this dataset.

descriptor_candidates.name: shape_aniso_S
descriptor_candidates.hypothesis: Adsorbate configurational entropy loss depends on shape anisotropy mismatch: molecules with high second-moment anisotropy (large spread among PMI1, PMI2, PMI3) lose more rotational entropy inside pores whose PBF (minimum free path) is small, so this anisotropy/PBF descriptor improves prediction of s_ads/s_gas beyond size-only descriptors.
descriptor_candidates.rationale: Inference: anisotropic molecules have orientation-dependent free volume in the pore; a small PBF penalizes misaligned orientations, freezing rotational degrees of freedom. PMI anisotropy normalized by PBF captures the mismatch between molecular shape and pore aperture geometry. This is a proposed mechanism, not a literature-verified relation for this dataset.
descriptor_candidates.falsification_criteria: If MAE of entropy loss/R does not improve when this descriptor augments the baseline 14 inputs, or if improvement vanishes when MW and Vol are ablated (indicating it only restates size), the rotational-freezing hypothesis is rejected.

descriptor_candidates.name: packing_potential_D
descriptor_candidates.hypothesis: Entropy loss is controlled by framework packing intensity and surface-field heterogeneity: denser frameworks with higher accessible-surface-to-pore-volume ratio (ASA/AV) and larger characteristic dimension dispersion (GeDi/SPAN) impose stronger and more heterogeneous adsorption fields, increasing entropy loss (lower s_ads/s_gas); a log-packed combination of these framework terms predicts residuals better than the raw 14-input network.
descriptor_candidates.rationale: Inference: entropy loss reflects the depth and spatial variation of the adsorption potential well. ASA/AV measures available surface per unit pore volume (surface-field strength proxy); GeDi/SPAN captures shape irregularity of the framework pore, which creates heterogeneous binding sites that quench translational freedom along the channel. Density is used only on its source numerical scale as a framework compactness ordering, without assigning physical units.
descriptor_candidates.falsification_criteria: If the descriptor's ranking correlation with entropy loss/R is below a weak threshold (e.g., |Spearman| < 0.2 across the dataset) and its inclusion yields no MAE reduction versus the 14-input baseline, the packing-heterogeneity mechanism is falsified; also falsified if performance is unchanged when density is randomly permuted.

descriptor_candidates.name: aperture_moment_tension
descriptor_candidates.hypothesis: Entropy loss is governed by aperture-to-molecule tightening modulated by framework free-path relaxation: when the largest framework dimension (lsd_f) exceeds the pore-limiting diameter (lsd_p), the pore is a channel with constrictions, and entropy loss grows; a larger PBF relative to framework geometric dispersion (GeDi) means straighter, less tortuous channels that partially restore translational freedom; higher free volume per molecular mass (Vol/MW) allows residual motion. The product descriptor predicts s_ads/s_gas residuals better than the 14-input baseline.
descriptor_candidates.rationale: Inference (not source evidence): constricted channels (lsd_f >> lsd_p) force passage through narrow windows, quenching translational entropy along the diffusion path; tortuosity (low PBF/GeDi) increases the number of distinct barriers crossed, further reducing entropy; Vol/MW acts as a per-unit-mass free-volume proxy. The log term compresses the aperture ratio into a smooth monotone penalty.
descriptor_candidates.falsification_criteria: Adding the descriptor to the 14-input network must reduce held-out MAE of entropy loss/R by >5% with non-overlapping resampling error bars versus the current best (0.5577). If Spearman correlation of the descriptor with entropy loss/R is |rho| < 0.2, or if improvement disappears when lsd_p and PBF are ablated, the constricted-channel mechanism is falsified for this dataset.

descriptor_candidates.name: surface_area_saturation
descriptor_candidates.hypothesis: Entropy loss saturates with adsorption-surface exposure per framework mass and with molecular span: frameworks combining high ASA with high density trap adsorbates on many closely spaced surfaces (losing nearly all gas-phase entropy), while bulky, wide-spanning molecules (large SPAN relative to MW) lose disproportionately more configurational entropy; the bounded exponential term plus a span/size term captures this saturating mechanism beyond the raw 14 inputs.
descriptor_candidates.rationale: Inference: adsorbate entropy loss approaches a limiting value as surface field density (ASA*density/AV) grows, suggesting a saturating (bounded) rather than linear response; the exp(-x) form encodes this asymptote. SPAN/MW distinguishes elongated molecules of equal mass, which lose more rotational entropy upon surface contact. Both terms are bounded, preventing pathological scaling.
descriptor_candidates.falsification_criteria: If the descriptor's inclusion yields no significant MAE improvement over the 0.5577 baseline, or if the exp term dominates performance while SPAN/MW is ablatable without loss (showing only surface density matters), the two-mechanism hypothesis is partially or fully falsified. Randomly permuting ASA across rows should destroy any improvement; if not, the descriptor is not encoding the claimed mechanism.

descriptor_candidates.name: inertia_volume_misfit
descriptor_candidates.hypothesis: Entropy loss peaks at a rotational-volume mismatch: the ratio of the largest principal moment times mass to molecular volume times the smallest moment measures how asymmetrically mass is distributed within the molecular envelope; this mismatch amplifies entropy loss only when the pore aperture is large relative to the molecule's span (entry feasible) and the framework is compact (density term bounded in [0,1)). The gated product descriptor improves prediction of entropy loss/R over the 14-input network.
descriptor_candidates.rationale: Inference: asymmetric inertia (high PMI3/PMI1 spread with high MW density) means rotational entropy is strongly quenched once the molecule is adsorbed, but only if the molecule can actually enter the pore (lsd_p/SPAN gating) and the framework offers a binding field (compactness). The minimum() gate expresses the 'entry-then-bind' sequence: neither factor alone should produce loss.
descriptor_candidates.falsification_criteria: If held-out MAE does not improve beyond the baseline within resampling uncertainty, or if the descriptor correlates with entropy loss equally well when the minimum() gate is replaced by either factor alone (indicating no genuine gating mechanism), the entry-then-rotational-quench hypothesis is rejected. Also falsified if PMI ablation removes all improvement, showing the descriptor merely restates molecular size via MW/Vol.

descriptor_candidates.name: free_path_freevolume_gate
descriptor_candidates.hypothesis: Entropy loss is controlled by the competition between free path length and free volume: when the minimum free path (PBF) times accessible molecular surface (LabuteASA) is large relative to molecular volume, the adsorbate retains translational freedom and loses little entropy; this protective factor is gated by the framework's pore-volume-per-mass (AV) relative to its density, so dense low-AV frameworks suppress the residual mobility. The gated bounded descriptor (values in (0,1)) improves MAE of entropy loss/R over the 14-input network and the two retained descriptors.
descriptor_candidates.rationale: Inference (not source evidence): entropy loss saturates when free volume per molecule falls below a thermal threshold; PBF sets the smallest wall-to-wall distance the molecule experiences, LabuteASA weights how much of its surface feels the wall field, and Vol normalizes this exposure. The AV/(AV+density) gate captures that pore volume only confers mobility when framework density does not pack the field too strongly. All quantities are bounded, avoiding unphysical scaling.
descriptor_candidates.falsification_criteria: Adding this descriptor must reduce held-out MAE of entropy loss/R below 0.5201 by a margin exceeding resampling error bars. If improvement vanishes when PBF or AV is ablated (showing it merely restates size/density already in the network), or if replacing the gate with a constant yields equal performance (no genuine gating), the free-path/free-volume competition mechanism is rejected for this dataset.

descriptor_candidates.name: elongation_tortuosity_product
descriptor_candidates.hypothesis: Entropy loss grows with the joint effect of molecular elongation and channel tortuosity: SPAN*GeDi/PBF^2 measures how many pore diameters long the molecule is compared with the narrowest free path (a tortuous-passage count), while the normalized middle moment PMI2/(PMI1+PMI3) distinguishes rod-like from disc-like shape in how rotational entropy is quenched; the descriptor predicts residuals beyond the retained packing and misfit descriptors.
descriptor_candidates.rationale: Inference: a molecule many free-paths long must thread through multiple constrictions, losing translational entropy stepwise (log of the tortuosity count encodes additive segment losses); rod-like molecules (middle moment small relative to extremes) align with channels and lose less rotational entropy than disc-like molecules, so the normalized PMI2 term should show a sign/shape-specific correlation. This separates shape-class effects from pure size, which the network already encodes.
descriptor_candidates.falsification_criteria: The descriptor must lower held-out MAE of entropy loss/R below 0.5201 significantly. Falsified if |Spearman| with entropy loss/R < 0.2, if PMI2 ablation removes all improvement (no shape-class mechanism), or if performance is unchanged when GeDi is randomly permuted (no tortuosity information).

descriptor_candidates.name: surface_field_screening
descriptor_candidates.hypothesis: Entropy loss is determined by the stronger of two independent quenching channels (a maximum, not a sum): (i) surface-field exposure per molecular volume (ASA/Vol), which quenches rotational/configurational entropy, or (ii) mass loading per accessible pore cross-section (MW/(lsd_f*lsd_p)), which quenches translational entropy in narrow channels; whichever channel dominates for a given framework/adsorbate pair sets the loss, with density screening the overall magnitude. This alternative-mechanism structure is falsifiably distinct from additive or product descriptors.
descriptor_candidates.rationale: Inference: rotational quenching depends on contact area per free volume, while translational quenching depends on how much mass must be accommodated in the channel cross-section; these are physically independent channels, so the binding-limiting (maximum) form, rather than a product, should track entropy loss in the regime where one channel dominates per system. The bounded density factor orders framework compactness on its source numerical scale without assigning unverified units.
descriptor_candidates.falsification_criteria: Descriptor must improve held-out MAE of entropy loss/R below 0.5201 beyond resampling uncertainty. The maximum-form hypothesis is specifically falsified if replacing maximum with a sum or with either branch alone gives equal or better performance (channels are not independent/limiting), or if ASA ablation and MW/lsd ablation each only partially remove improvement in a way inconsistent with a dominant-channel regime structure.
